summary: Reviewed 3 modified files (src/config/config.constants.ts, src/server/routes/config.ts, src/config/config.ts). OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium finding noted (token trimming side-effect). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium | A04 — Insecure Design (token trimming side-effect) | src/server/routes/config.ts lines 273–280. The token field is length-checked on token.trim() and then stored as cleanToken = token.trim(). If a user submits a token with leading/trailing whitespace (e.g. a paste from a clipboard with a trailing newline), the stored token will silently differ from what was submitted. If the original token was already at the 500-char limit, trimming could shorten it, causing authentication failures with the remote Git host. Recommendation: either reject tokens that contain leading/trailing whitespace (HTTP 400, 'token must not contain leading or trailing whitespace') or document that trimming is intentional. The current behaviour is consistent with the other fields (label, id also trim), but tokens are sensitive secrets where silent truncation is more consequential.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures (PASS): Tokens are stored in plaintext in config.json, which is the expected design for a local developer tool using PATs. The saveConfigField() function applies chmod 600 after every write (config.ts line 320–322), restricting access to the file owner on POSIX systems. All API responses mask tokens to '****' + last-4 chars. No hardcoded secrets in any of the three modified files.

A09 — Security Logging (PASS): Audit log entries are generated for create, update, and delete credential operations via errorLogManager.append(). The token value is explicitly excluded from all audit log messages — only id, label, and host are logged. This is correct.

A03 — Injection (PASS): No injection vectors identified. The host field rejects '/', '\', null bytes, and whitespace via regex before the length check. All credential fields are stored as JSON config values — not interpolated into shell commands, SQL queries, or template engines within the modified code.

A06 — Vulnerable Components (PASS): No new third-party dependencies were introduced by this WP. Only named constants were added to config.constants.ts and imported into existing modules. No CVE review required.

Full OWASP Top 10 sweep — no Critical or High issues found across A01–A10. The named-constant extraction is a net security improvement: it eliminates magic numbers and ensures the API route handler and config parser enforce identical bounds from a single source of truth.

comments.note: config.constants.ts — The new GitCredentialEntry section follows the established file convention precisely (section-header comment, JSDoc with rationale, named exports). The host limit (253) is explicitly tied to RFC 1035 in the docstring, which is excellent — a future maintainer doesn't need to look it up. No issues.

routes/config.ts — Validation ordering is correct and consistent: (1) type/presence check, (2) character-validity check (for host only — path separators/whitespace/null bytes), (3) length check. This ordering means the whitespace check fires before the host length check, which is correct (a whitespace-padded host is rejected for the right reason before it ever reaches the length gate). The id length check is correctly conditional on typeof id === 'string', avoiding a double-check path.

config.ts parseGitCredentials() — The fieldLimits array approach (lines 213–226) is a clean, DRY way to apply the four checks without repeating the conditional structure. The diagnostic error message format (includes 'got N') is appropriate for a startup/parse error context and intentionally differs from the API error format — this is correct and was noted by the Developer.

[documentation-forward] config.ts parseGitCredentials() applies .trim() in the length-check loop (line 220) to measure trimmed length, but the final return (line 237) is 'value as GitCredentialEntry[]' — the raw (un-trimmed) strings from config.json. This means a config.json entry with padded whitespace (e.g. '  my-id  ') will pass the length check on the trimmed form but be stored in-memory with the whitespace. This is a pre-existing design choice (the function was not responsible for normalizing values) but becomes more visible now that trim() is explicitly used in the length path. constraints.md should note that parseGitCredentials() does not normalize field values — consumers should trim before use, or a future WP should align the normalization behavior with the route handler (which explicitly produces cleanId/cleanLabel/cleanHost/cleanToken).

[documentation-forward] The token field (and id/label) are silently trimmed before storage in the PUT /api/config/credentials route handler (cleanToken = token.trim()). This is intentional normalization (clipboard paste with trailing newline is a common UX case) but is undocumented. constraints.md should add a note under the Per-Field Length Limits table clarifying that the API trims leading/trailing whitespace from id, label, and token before storing, and that the host field instead rejects whitespace outright. This resolves the Security Auditor's medium finding (A04) without a code change.
